# Hygiene

<!-- generated by scripts/hygiene-doc.ts from packages/contract/src/hygiene-catalogue.ts: edit the catalogue, then `bun scripts/hygiene-doc.ts` -->

Hygiene is the factory's standing check on a project's health: probes read a throwaway checkout of the default branch, and
what they find becomes a signal, then an Issue like any other. The probes are one catalogue in code. This page, the project
page's Hygiene tab and `factory read project-hygiene <name>` render that one list, so they cannot disagree.

## How a pass runs

| Pass | When | What runs |
|-|-|-|
| Weekly (full) | a project's newest full pass is a week old, or sooner for a busy repo | every probe the project has on, the project's own probes, and the document judgment |
| Monthly (full) | an idle repo's newest full pass is 30 days old | the same as the weekly full pass |
| Steady | an idle repo's newest weekly or steady pass is a week old | every probe but the ones marked `idle: monthly` (`deps`) and no judgment |
| Daily | the newest pass of any scope is a day old | only the probes marked `daily` below, no judgment |

- **An idle repo goes slower.** A repo whose default branch has had no commit for 30 days (read from its
  newest pass) is swept in full monthly and steady in between: the `deps` refresh and the document judgment wait for the month,
  `advisories` and every other probe keep their cadence, and a commit that lands before a steady pass makes it a full one.
- **A busy repo goes sooner.** A daily pass becomes a full one when 30 or more commits landed since the last full pass and that
  pass is at least two days old.
- **Read again before filing.** A sweep takes minutes and the default branch moves meanwhile. When it is no longer the commit swept,
  the red findings of the probes that only read tracked files (cost `file`, `agentsmd` among them) are read again at the new
  head and only what it still raises is filed; a finding it no longer raises reads green, and the run says at which commit.
- **One project per tick.** Full passes come before daily ones, never-swept projects first, then the oldest.
- **One Issue per pass.** A pass of one repo files its findings as one signal and one Issue: a section per finding, each headed
  by its key, so each key still heals, reopens and is judged by itself (`loop_findings` keeps a row per key). The Issue is
  closed as healed only when every key in it is green; while one is still red it is told which keys are.
- **Budget.** At most 3 probe findings and 5 sections in all per pass, probes ranked in the catalogue's order; the rest are
  named in the pass record, never dropped. A finder that mostly ends dropped or cancelled stops filing for 14 days.
- **Settings.** `FACTORY_HYGIENE_EVERY_MS` (the week) and `FACTORY_HYGIENE_RETRY_MS` (`apps/server/src/app/loops/settings.ts`, set in the env file); the daily pass is once a day.
- **The seat.** Every signal carries a `Seat:` line. A finding's Issue starts on the light seat whatever its size: the probe that
  found it turning green proves the fix, and a light lead that struggles is moved up once.
- **One detector per fact.** A red default branch is filed by the intake's `signals.github.checks` where a project turns it on; the
  `check` probe runs (in a test slot) only for a project without it. A slow route answer is filed by the Kuma monitor alone.

## The dependency refresh

The `deps` and `advisories` probes read every ecosystem (`package.json`, Cargo, Python, Swift, Dockerfile base images, GitHub
Actions) and fold what they read into **one finding, `deps`, per repo**: a section and an upgrade plan per ecosystem and the
procedure once. It is filed only when it clears the bar; versions still inside their cooldown (7 days, 14 for a major) never count.

| It is filed when | Default |
|-|-|
| a high or critical advisory has a fixed version | always |
| a runtime dependency is a major behind (non-dev npm, Cargo, Python, Swift, a Docker base image) | always; dev tools and GitHub Actions do not file alone |
| a runtime dependency is a minor or more behind and its latest is at least this old | 30 days |
| this many dependencies are behind in all, dev tools and patches included | 10 |

Below the bar nothing is filed: the `deps` run on the Hygiene tab says what is behind. An advisory with no fixed version is never
filed; the `advisories` run lists it and the next pass reads it again. A project changes the numbers under `hygiene` (see below),
with its reason.

## What happens to a finding

A finding is its key (`links:docs/a.md`, `check`) and the Issues that key filed. Its state is read from the newest of
those Issues and from the next pass's verdict, never stored.

| The probe says | The newest Issue of the key is | The pass does |
|-|-|-|
| red | none, or closed healed, dropped or cancelled | files a section of the pass's Issue (a new Issue when none is open) |
| red | open | nothing: the Issue is the finding's life |
| red | closed done, within 29 days | reopens that Issue with the evidence of its red keys; no second Issue |
| red | closed done and already reopened twice | leaves it to a person, and says so on the Hygiene tab |
| green (ran, did not raise the key), every key of the Issue | queued or settling: no lead has started | closes it as healed, with the probe's run as the reason |
| green, every key of the Issue | a lead is working or waiting | tells the lead once; the lead decides |
| green, some keys; others still red | open | tells the Issue which keys are green and which are not; it stays open |
| green | in its Watch, or closed | nothing |

**A scripted fix comes first.** A probe whose catalogue entry has a `fix` (below) is fixed by script before anything is filed: the
script runs in the pass's throwaway checkout, then the same probe runs again. What it no longer raises files nothing, and an
Issue of that key that no lead has started is closed as healed by the table above. A fix that failed, or left something red,
leaves the finding as it was with the script's output on it, and the Issue goes to a light lead as always. Every attempt is
listed on the Hygiene tab (`fixes` of `factory read project-hygiene <name>`).

A run that was skipped or failed says nothing about a key, so it never heals. The document judgment never heals: it reads a
few documents, and absence proves nothing. Every action is recorded on the pass and listed on the Hygiene tab.

### check

`make check` on the default branch in a throwaway checkout, inside a test slot; red is one finding with the tail of the output, confirmed in the project's own checkout when that is clean at the same commit. A project whose `signals.github.checks` is on has its red default branch filed by the intake and skips this probe, so the one fact has one detector.

- **Default:** on for every project.
- **Runs:** in the weekly pass; runs the project's own make target.
- **Silence it:** Set `hygiene: { check: false, reason: <why> }` when the gate needs a lab this host lacks; a red `doctor` skips it on its own.

### advisories

Known security advisories of severity high and up in the lockfiles: `bun audit` for a `bun.lock`, `osv-scanner` for `Cargo.lock`, `uv.lock`, `requirements*.txt` and `Package.resolved`. An advisory with a fixed version files the `deps` refresh; one with none is listed on the tab and read again every pass, never filed.

- **Default:** on when detection finds what it reads: a lockfile of one of those kinds is tracked; the Cargo, Python and Swift ones are skipped on a host without `osv-scanner`.
- **Runs:** in the weekly pass; runs an analyzer or asks a registry.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### links

Relative links in the living Markdown documents that point at a file that does not exist.

- **Default:** on for every project.
- **Runs:** in the daily pass and the weekly one; reads tracked files.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### retired

The repo's own retired-words check (`scripts/retired-words.ts`) over the living documents `make check` does not scan.

- **Default:** on when detection finds what it reads: the repo has `scripts/retired-words.ts`.
- **Runs:** in the daily pass and the weekly one; reads tracked files.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### project

The `project.yaml` itself, linted like `factory project check`: keys nothing reads, a `make` target the Makefile lacks, a header that cites a missing document, a `doctor` or `verify` target the Makefile has but the file does not name, deploy targets with mode `none`, constants without a stated reason.

- **Default:** on when detection finds what it reads: the repo has a `project.yaml`.
- **Runs:** in the daily pass and the weekly one; reads tracked files.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### deps

Outdated dependencies and the advisories above, as one refresh per repo: `bun outdated` for a `package.json`, and the versions pinned in `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml` or `requirements*.txt`, `Package.swift`, Dockerfile base images and GitHub Actions `uses:` lines. One finding `deps` is filed only when the refresh clears the bar (below); it carries a section and an upgrade plan per ecosystem (versions younger than 7 days, 14 for a major, held back; patches and minors, packages that move together, and each major in batches) and the procedure a light lead follows. Below the bar nothing is filed and the Hygiene tab names what is behind.

- **Default:** on when detection finds what it reads: a package file of one of those kinds is tracked; every ecosystem is one finding.
- **Runs:** in the weekly pass, and only monthly on an idle repo; runs an analyzer or asks a registry.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.
- **Scripted fix:** For `bun`: each patch or minor past its cooldown that the root `package.json` declares is set with `bun add <name>@<version>` (an exact pin stays exact), then the repo's check runs in a test slot. On green, a `chore(deps)` commit: pushed to the default branch of a repo that ships by push, or, for one that ships by pull request, opened as a pull request inside the repo's merge window, merged once its CI and the merge guard are green (a red CI closes it). Neither deploys: the next ship of the repo does. A red check, a major, a held version, a workspace package and every other ecosystem go to a lead; the check's output is on the Issue.

### ci

The workflow files: a private repo runs on `[self-hosted, vps]` and never a hosted runner, `uses:` lines are pinned to a version or a sha, and, for a project whose `checks` says `ci: true`, a workflow calls the same `make` target the project names as its full check.

- **Default:** on when detection finds what it reads: the repo has `.github/workflows/*.yml`.
- **Runs:** in the daily pass and the weekly one; reads tracked files.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### agentsmd

The repo contract for agent files (dotfiles `docs/agents-md.md`): no `CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md`, no `@imports` in an `AGENTS.md`, no `ask` rules in a checked-in `.claude/settings.json`. A `CLAUDE.md` under a `fixtures/` directory is a documented benchmark fixture and is not a finding.

- **Default:** on when detection finds what it reads: the repo has an `AGENTS.md`, a `CLAUDE.md` or a `.claude/settings.json`.
- **Runs:** in the daily pass and the weekly one; reads tracked files.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### readme

Every command (`make <target>`, `bun run <script>`) and path a `README.md` names exists in the repo.

- **Default:** on when detection finds what it reads: the repo has a `README.md`.
- **Runs:** in the daily pass and the weekly one; reads tracked files.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### stale

Remote branches merged into the default branch or untouched for 30 days, and leftover worktrees of branches that are gone.

- **Default:** on for every project.
- **Runs:** in the daily pass and the weekly one; reads tracked files.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.
- **Scripted fix:** Deletes the remote branches merged into the default branch (`git push origin --delete`), prunes worktrees git calls prunable and removes the merged ones that are idle (`git worktree remove`, never `--force`: a dirty or locked one stays). The worktree of a lead (branch `factory/<issue>-<attempt>`, or its directory `factory-<issue>-<attempt>` once the branch is gone) is never touched: its finalization removes it. On the remote and the project checkout at once. Branches only untouched for 30 days and worktrees only untouched are not deleted: they stay a finding for a lead.

### deadcode

Unused files, exports and dependencies of a JavaScript or TypeScript repo (fallow, the analyzer behind the `analyze` skill); only the top findings.

- **Default:** on when detection finds what it reads: the repo has a `package.json` and `fallow` is installed on the host.
- **Runs:** in the weekly pass; runs an analyzer or asks a registry.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### runrules

The owner's rules for what runs on the Mac mini (restart policy, memory limit, port binding, healthcheck, registered jobs), read from the files before a change reaches the host.

- **Default:** on when detection finds what it reads: the repo has a root `mini-services.yaml`, or a deploy target on host `mini` in `project.yaml`.
- **Runs:** in the daily pass and the weekly one; reads tracked files.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### browser

The owner's browser rule for suites and agent tooling: Playwright's bundled headless shell unless a line states why not, never headed, a command-line tool and a skill instead of an MCP server.

- **Default:** on for every project.
- **Runs:** in the daily pass and the weekly one; reads tracked files.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### context

The byte budgets of the files an agent loads every turn: 12,000 bytes for the root `AGENTS.md`, 8,000 for a nested one.

- **Default:** on when detection finds what it reads: the repo has an `AGENTS.md`.
- **Runs:** in the daily pass and the weekly one; reads tracked files.
- **Silence it:** Name it under `hygiene.skip` in `project.yaml` with a reason; the pass shows the reason.

### probe

The project's own probes: each is `make <target>` in the throwaway checkout, red on any exit but 0, filed as `probe:<name>`.

- **Default:** only where the project asks: the project lists it under `hygiene.probes` in `project.yaml`.
- **Runs:** in the weekly pass; runs the project's own make target.
- **Silence it:** Remove it from `hygiene.probes`.

### judgment

One agent reads the living documents whose code moved on since they were last edited, and those edited lately, and files `stale` and `slop` findings; the factory checks every answer again.

- **Default:** on for every project.
- **Runs:** in the weekly pass, and only monthly on an idle repo; one model call on the cheap seat.
- **Silence it:** Not switchable: it takes at most two sections of a pass and a held class stops it.

## For a repo author

- **See what runs.** `factory read project-hygiene <name>` or the project's Hygiene tab: each probe with its last run,
  the findings that stand and what became of each.
- **Silence a probe** with its reason; the reason is required and the pass shows it:

```yaml
hygiene:
  skip:
    - { probe: deadcode, reason: generated code is imported by the build, not by source }
  check: false # the gate needs a lab this host lacks
  reason: needs the device farm
```

- **Move the bar or the idle cadence** with the reason that explains it (`idleAfterDays: 0` is never idle):

```yaml
hygiene:
  deps: { runtimeStaleDays: 14, behindRows: 6 }
  idleAfterDays: 60
  reason: a runtime that ships to users weekly; a long-lived branch model
```

- **Add your own probe**: a make target that exits 0 when green, and `hygiene: { probes: [{ name, target }] }`. It runs weekly,
  one finding `probe:<name>` with the output tail.
- **Clear a finding.** Fix what it names, or for a false positive silence the probe with a reason, or close its Issue as
  dropped with the reason (a class that is mostly dropped stops filing).
- **Check the project file before you push** with `factory project check`: it is the lint the `project` probe runs.
- **Coverage** is not a built-in probe. A repo that wants it declares a probe whose target fails under a floor.
